info.name: World Cup Prediction API
info.description:
Postman collection for Project Part B. Set baseUrl to [http://localhost:5000](http://localhost:5000) and token after login/register.

## Flow 1: New User Prediction Flow

1. Register a new user using POST /api/auth/register.
    
2. Login using POST /api/auth/login and copy the JWT token.
    
3. Fetch available matches using GET /api/matches.
    
4. Save one match ID into the matchId collection variable.
    
5. Create a prediction using POST /api/predictions.
    
6. Verify the prediction using GET /api/predictions/mine.
    
7. Check that the leaderboard updates using GET /api/leaderboard.
    

### This flow proves:

- User management
    
- Authentication
    
- Read matches from DB
    
- Create prediction
    
- Fetch by logged-in user
    
- Leaderboard/statistics
    

## Flow 2: Manage Prediction Flow

1. Login using POST /api/auth/login.
    
2. Fetch user predictions using GET /api/predictions/mine.
    
3. Save one prediction ID into the predictionId collection variable.
    
4. Update the prediction using PUT /api/predictions/{{predictionId}}.
    
5. Verify the updated prediction using GET /api/predictions/mine.
    
6. Delete the prediction using DELETE /api/predictions/{{predictionId}}.
    
7. Verify deletion using GET /api/predictions/mine.
    

### This flow proves:

- StartFragmentRead
    
- Update
    
- Delete
    
- Protected routes
    
- User-specific data
    
- Relation between prediction and matchEndFragment
    

## External API Flow

The Featured Matches page calls GET /api/external/country/:name through the backend.  
The backend uses the Open-Meteo Geocoding API to return capital/city location, country code, timezone, latitude, and longitude.  
Example:

GET /api/external/country/Mexico
